key_insight: A reduced-basis hybrid ML framework combining TBNN and UDEs can learn frame-invariant viscoelastic constitutive laws from shear data and generalize to more complex flows.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables data-efficient digital-twin rheology models that can be embedded directly in CFD solvers for predicting viscoelastic fluid behavior in engineering geometries.
method: Reduced-dimensional tensor basis to improve physical consistency and numerical stability
UDE constitutive law embedded in an open-source finite-volume CFD solver
Trained on synthetic oscillatory-shear data from established viscoelastic models
evidence_signal: The models were evaluated by extrapolating from shear training data to unseen extensional flows and benchmark 2D/3D cases such as the 4:1 sudden contraction and cross-slot, where they captured key elastic-instability features but with decreasing accuracy under stronger extrapolation.
watch_item: Performance degrades as conditions move farther from the shear-only training regime, so robust deployment likely requires additional stress/normal-stress data and careful validation in high-Deborah-number flows.
paper_title: Harnessing Machine Learning for Hybrid Constitutive Modelling of Viscoelastic Fluid Flows in Computational Rheology
